ai.title: Fix auth code expiry parsing
ai.summary: Web login page now uses `parseAuthCode` and `isAuthCodeExpired` from `@/app/onboard/_helpers` instead of manual string splitting and `parseInt`. This prevents crashes or incorrect expiry checks when auth code formats vary or contain unexpected values. Scope covers both `freebuff/web/src/app/login/page.tsx` and `web/src/app/login/page.tsx`.

eli5.text: When you sign into the web app using an auth code, the login page now reads the expiry time from that code more carefully instead of cutting it out by hand. If you paste an auth code that has an unexpected format or missing pieces, you will no longer get a crash or a misleading 'expired' message; the page will simply tell you the code has expired only when it actually has. This fix is live today in both the freebuff web and main web login flows.

ai.title: Next 15.5.16, MiniMax M2.7, env fix
ai.summary: Upgraded Next.js to 15.5.16 in web/package.json and freebuff/web/package.json. Added caniuse-lite to root package.json. Refactored ensureEnvDefault in packages/internal/src/env.ts to apply outside CI checks. Updated home-client.tsx to include MiniMax M2.7 in model FAQ.

eli5.text: If you open Freebuff today, the web app loads on the latest version of Next.js (15.5.16), which is a behind-the-scenes upgrade that keeps the site building and running correctly. The FAQ on the homepage now lists MiniMax M2.7 as an additional coding model you can pick, alongside DeepSeek V4 Pro and Kimi K2.6, with clearer notes about daily session limits and each model's trade-offs. Separately, a small fix makes the app's environment setup work the same way whether tests run on a developer's computer or on the automated servers that build and test the code.

ai.title: Update Web FAQ model list and data training policy
ai.summary: Refactored the model list in the Web FAQ to a bulleted format and removed specific session limit details. Updated the data training policy to clarify that third-party training occurs only if users select models explicitly labeled 'Collects data for training'. Changes apply to freebuff/web/src/app/home-client.tsx.

eli5.text: The list of available assistants in the help section now simply spells out which ones collect data for training, and the question about session limits was removed. If you open the help page, you'll see the model names in a bulleted list instead of one long paragraph, and the note about training now states clearly that only models labeled as collecting data for training will use your conversations to teach themselves. Today, visitors to the site will read the updated help text as soon as they reload the page.

ai.title: Disable CLI diff rendering
ai.summary: DiffViewer returns null when RENDER_DIFFS is false, disabling CLI diff rendering. Implemented via hardcoded boolean flag in cli/src/components/tools/diff-viewer.tsx. Affects CLI tool output surfaces.

eli5.text: When the command line shows you a list of changes, it will now hide the side-by-side colored diff view and simply return nothing instead. The tool that draws those change previews now checks an internal on/off switch that has been flipped to off, so any surface that relied on it gets an empty result. If you were expecting to see the formatted additions and removals in your terminal, you will not see them anymore. The change is live today.

ai.title: Revert deterministic tool call ids
ai.summary: Reverts deterministic tool call id generation in `packages/agent-runtime`. `createToolCallIdGenerator` removed from `run-programmatic-step.ts`, `tools/stream-parser.ts`, and `tools/tool-executor.ts`. Callers now use `crypto.randomUUID()` or `generateCompactId()` directly. `util/tool-call-id.ts` deleted.

eli5.text: The assistant used to give each tool call a predictable name based on what tools had already been used, which helped keep things stable and repeatable. This change removes that predictable naming system and goes back to generating random identifiers for each tool call instead. You would notice this in the background processing of the assistant's actions, where tool calls are now tracked with random IDs rather than structured ones, making the internal tracking less consistent but simpler.

ai.title: CLI version 1.0.670 release roll-up
ai.summary: Bumped the codebuff CLI package version from 1.0.669 to 1.0.670 in cli/release/package.json as a packaging release cut. This release bundles the prior days user-facing changes: auth code parsing hardened to lastIndexOf extraction and request-origin login URLs, stale Freebuff session auto-takeover via freebuff-instance-owner PID tracking, session-ended restart options, SIGNUP_FREE_CREDITS_GRANT of 500 replacing DEFAULT_FREE_CREDITS_GRANT monthly grants, and CLI model selector tier grouping with the premium session counter moved to the waiting room title. The version bump itself touches only the version field with no source changes.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json: version field changed from 1.0.669 to 1.0.670 (release-bump commit c696d670). Surrounding commits on 2026-05-06/07 shipped auth code parsing fixes, stale session auto-takeover, Freebuff session restart banner, signup free credits replacing monthly grants, and CLI model selector tier grouping.

eli5.text: This release improves how you sign in and use Freebuff CLI sessions. When you log in, the system now correctly handles account names that contain dots, so fewer logins break at the last step. If you leave a session running and it stops responding, Freebuff will automatically reclaim it instead of leaving you stuck waiting, and you will see a new on-screen option to restart the same chat or pick a different AI model when a session ends. New users now get a single 500-credit welcome bonus at signup instead of a smaller monthly credit, giving a bigger initial boost to start building. The model picker in the terminal now organizes AI models into clear Premium and Unlimited groups, and the main waiting-room screen shows how many premium sessions you have left up front so it is easier to choose what you want. Freebuff has also added the MiniMax M2.7 model to its list of available AI options. Finally, the web FAQ and data-training policy were updated to make model choices and privacy practices clearer, and CLI diff output can now be turned off with a simple setting, which is useful in busy terminals where diff text adds noise.

ai.title: Freebuff version bumped to 0.0.81
ai.summary: Version 0.0.81 is released as a packaging-only bump of the freebuff CLI manifest, following the release-bump convention. This cut bundles the preceding day's fixes and improvements, including auth code expiry parsing on the Web login page, Next.js upgrade to 15.5.16, DiffViewer flag, MiniMax M2.7 FAQ update, and the revert of deterministic tool call id generation.
ai.evidence: freebuff/cli/release/package.json: version bumped from 0.0.80 to 0.0.81 in the release manifest. This is a release-bump commit with no source changes.

eli5.text: This release adds support for the MiniMax M2.7 AI model, upgrades the web platform to the latest Next.js version for better performance, and fixes login issues that could cause errors when signing in. The login flow now correctly handles authentication code expiration, preventing crashes when codes have unexpected formats. The web FAQ has been updated with a clearer bulleted list of available models and a revised data training policy that clarifies only models labeled as collecting training data will use your information. CLI diff rendering can now be toggled off, and tool call identification has been reverted to a simpler random generation method for improved reliability. Upgrading gives you access to the new MiniMax M2.7 model, more stable logins, a cleaner model selection interface, and better control over terminal output display.

ai.title: Revert duplicate reviewer agent card fix
ai.summary: Reverted changes to `getAgentBaseName` and `moveSpawnAgentBlock` that caused duplicate reviewer agent cards. Removed underscore-to-hyphen normalization in `cli/src/utils/message-block-helpers.ts` and stripped `realAgentType` propagation from `cli/src/utils/sdk-event-handlers.ts`, `cli/src/utils/spawn-agent-matcher.ts`, and `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts`. Restores original agent ID resolution and block movement logic.

eli5.text: If you ever saw the command-line assistant show your conversation history with the same helper agent listed twice, that mix-up is back: this change undoes the adjustment that had prevented duplicate reviewer agent cards from appearing, so the assistant is once again using its original method for telling agents apart and moving their message blocks into place. You, the person running the assistant in a terminal, would notice that the duplicated cards can reappear in your session log, and the assistant will resolve agent identities the way it did before this rollback. The fix is live today for anyone using the CLI as of this snapshot, including the test files that previously locked in the anti-duplicate behavior.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.671 release bundle ships reviewer card revert
ai.summary: Version 1.0.671 is a packaging bump in cli/release/package.json, advancing the codebuff package from 1.0.670 to 1.0.671 with no source files modified. This release bundles the prior revert that removed underscore-to-hyphen normalization in getAgentBaseName and stripped realAgentType propagation across message-block-helpers, sdk-event-handlers, spawn-agent-matcher, and the agent-runtime tool-executor, restoring original agent ID resolution and block movement logic. The bump follows the release-bump convention used to lock a coherent set of CLI improvements into the released bundle.
ai.evidence: Diff shows a single-line version change from 1.0.670 to 1.0.671 in the only modified file, cli/release/package.json. The commit metadata tags it as a release-bump with no source files changed. The accompanying release notes confirm 1.0.671 contains the prior revert of duplicate reviewer agent card fixes, restoring original agent ID resolution and block movement logic.

eli5.text: This release fixes a glitch where duplicate reviewer cards could appear during code reviews, restoring clean navigation and preventing confusion when switching between agent views. The update reverts problematic naming and block-movement logic that caused reviewer entries to multiply, ensuring each agent type displays only once in your terminal interface. You will no longer see repeated reviewer panels interrupting your workflow or conflicting agent identifiers when running multi-step reviews. Upgrading smooths out the review experience so agent cards behave predictably during interactive sessions.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.82 release packaging bump
ai.summary: Bumped the `freebuff` CLI package version from 0.0.81 to 0.0.82 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` as a release cut. The preceding user-visible work, the revert of the duplicate reviewer agent card fix (dropping underscore-to-hyphen normalization in `cli/src/utils/message-block-helpers.ts` and stripping `realAgentType` propagation across `cli/src/utils/sdk-event-handlers.ts`, `cli/src/utils/spawn-agent-matcher.ts`, and `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts`), is now locked into the released CLI bundle. This is a packaging-only update; no source files changed beyond the version field.
ai.evidence: Single-line version bump in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` changing `0.0.81` to `0.0.82`, categorized as a release-bump commit.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.82 restores correct agent behavior after a recent change accidentally caused duplicate reviewer agent cards to appear during multi-step coding sessions, so task orchestration now displays and tracks each assistant role clearly without visual duplication. The fix reverts identifier renaming that was converting underscores to hyphens in agent IDs and stops internal agent-type metadata from being passed through rendering layers, returning the system to its original agent ID resolution and block-movement logic. Upgrading to this version gives you a cleaner, more accurate agent workspace where subagents and reviewers are shown once and behave predictably again, eliminating confusing repeated cards when complex tasks spawn specialized helper agents.

ai.title: CLI login URL origin derives from NEXTPUBLICCODEBUFFAPPURL
ai.summary: CLI login URL origin now derives from `NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL`, falling back to request origin or hardcoded production domain. Replaces raw request-origin derivation to prevent apex/www host bouncing during OAuth. Covers `freebuff/web/src/app/api/auth/cli/code/route.ts` and `web/src/app/api/auth/cli/code/route.ts` via new `_origin.ts` helper. `allowLocalhost` flag enabled when `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT` is not `prod`.

eli5.text: When you log into the command-line version of the app on a new computer, the website will now always send you back to the correct main address, instead of sometimes bouncing you to a slightly wrong version of it during the OAuth login step. The system now reads the official app address from a configured setting first, and only falls back to the address it saw in your request or a hardcoded default if that setting is missing. This fix is already live today and applies to both the free and paid versions of the web app.

ai.title: Restore subagent alias card matching
ai.summary: CLI restores subagent alias card matching by normalizing agent names with underscores to hyphens in `getAgentBaseName`. The `realAgentType` is now passed through `moveSpawnAgentBlock` and `resolveSpawnAgentToReal` to ensure agent cards display the correct type. This fixes matching issues in `cli/src/utils/message-block-helpers.ts` and `cli/src/utils/sdk-event-handlers.ts`.

eli5.text: When you use the command-line assistant and it spawns a helper agent, the helper's name and type now display correctly even if the name uses underscores instead of hyphens. Previously, names like 'file_picker' wouldn't match properly when looking up the agent card to show in your terminal, causing the helper to appear with the wrong or missing label. Now names are normalized during lookup and the actual agent type is passed through the whole process so the right display name shows up. This fix is live today in the CLI.

ai.title: Dynamic agent selection by model
ai.summary: CLI now resolves freebuff agents dynamically based on selected model via new `freebuff-agent-selection.ts` utility. Replaced static `AGENT_MODE_TO_ID` lookup with `getAgentIdForMode()` helper that maps LITE mode to model-specific root agents (e.g., `base2-free-kimi`, `base2-free-deepseek`). Added dedicated reviewer agents (`code-reviewer-kimi`, `code-reviewer-deepseek`, `code-reviewer-minimax`) and updated base2 factory to accept `freeCodeReviewerAgentId`. Core logic moved from `local-agent-registry` to shared constants, enabling per-model Gemini thinker gating via `canFreebuffModelSpawnGeminiThinker`.

eli5.text: When you ask the free Codebuff assistant to review or work on your code, it now picks the version of its helper tools that matches the specific AI model you selected at that moment, for example, if you choose the DeepSeek-powered free assistant, the code review helper is the DeepSeek-tuned reviewer, and if you pick the Kimi-powered one, you get the Kimi-tuned reviewer. The default free option still uses the fast MiniMax model and its matching reviewer unless you specifically switch models. This means the helper that gives you feedback on your code can now be tailored to the same AI that is driving the session, instead of using one generic helper for everyone.

ai.title: Allow legacy code-reviewer-lite models
ai.summary: Added code-reviewer-lite to FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS in common/src/constants/free-agents.ts. Legacy freebuff clients spawned this agent under provider-specific free roots before dedicated reviewer IDs existed. Maps to FREEBUFF_MINIMAX_MODEL_ID, FREEBUFF_KIMI_MODEL_ID, and FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL_ID. Ensures backward compatibility for older agent invocations.

eli5.text: Older client apps that still ask for the code-reviewer-lite assistant will now get served again. Those apps were built before reviewers had their own names and relied on generic provider-specific roots, so this maps the legacy request back to the matching models for MiniMax, KI, and DeepSeek. If you look, you'll see the reviewer now accepts requests from those older clients without error.

ai.title: Add deepseek to base2-free free mode agent models
ai.summary: Added FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL_ID to the base2-free set in FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS. Root orchestrator now routes deepseek alongside minimax and glm. Change scoped to common/src/constants/free-agents.ts. Separate base2-free-kimi and base2-free-deepseek agent sets remain unchanged.

eli5.text: If you use the free tier of the service, the assistant can now include a DeepSeek model when it picks which AI helper to run with. The free mode that previously only mixed Minimax and GLM models now also routes to DeepSeek alongside them, while the separate dedicated free DeepSeek and free Kimi mode sets stay the same. The change is live today in the common code that powers the free mode selection.

ai.title: Add FREEBUFFKIMIMODELID to FREEMODEAGENTMODELS
ai.summary: Added FREEBUFF_KIMI_MODEL_ID to FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS in common/src/constants/free-agents.ts. Enables Kimi model availability for free mode agents. Covers core constants.

eli5.text: If you use the free version of the assistant, you can now pick the Kimi model alongside the existing free options like MiniMax, GLM, and DeepSeek V4 Pro. The free-mode model list had a small addition that makes Kimi available to free users, and a paired test confirms it. Nothing about the pricing or which accounts qualify changed, free users simply gained one more model they can switch to.

ai.title: Waiting room displays used premium sessions
ai.summary: Waiting room screen switched from displaying remaining premium sessions to showing used count out of total limit. Replaced `premiumLeft` calculation with `isPremiumExhausted` check and `formattedSharedPremiumUsed` string. Text now reads 'X of Y premium sessions used today' with dynamic padding to prevent layout shifts during loading. Internal UI change affecting `cli/src/components/waiting-room-screen.tsx`.

eli5.text: When you land on the waiting room screen before picking a model, you'll now see how many premium sessions you've already used out of the daily total, like "2 of 5 premium sessions used today", instead of how many were left. The count is padded with spaces so the line doesn't jump or shift width while it's loading, keeping the title centered. This affects anyone hitting the waiting room screen while premium sessions are in use.

ai.title: Add OpenCode runner to BuffBench
ai.summary: OpenCode CLI added as external agent for BuffBench evaluations. New `OpenCodeRunner` spawns `opencode run` with JSON output, defaulting to `opencode/kimi-k2.6` unless `OPENCODE_MODEL` overrides it. Supported via `external:opencode` agent ID in `run-buffbench.ts` and `agent-runner.ts`, with README install instructions requiring `OPENCODE_API_KEY`.

eli5.text: If you run BuffBench evaluations against coding agents, you can now point it at OpenCode CLI using the identifier external:opencode. The suite spawns OpenCode with a default model of opencode/kimi-k2.6, overridable by your OPENCODE_MODEL environment variable, and uses JSON output plus your OPENCODE_API_KEY to authenticate. The supported external agent list, docs install steps, and a fallback error message now all accept opencode.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.672 release bundles CLI login, model-based agent routing
ai.summary: Version 1.0.672 of the codebuff CLI package ships in cli/release/package.json, bundling fixes and features already landed earlier today. The CLI login URL origin now derives from NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL (falling back to request origin or the production domain) to prevent apex/www host bouncing during OAuth, and per-model agent resolution replaces the static AGENT_MODE_TO_ID lookup via a new freebuff-agent-selection.ts utility that maps LITE mode to model-specific root agents and adds dedicated code-reviewer-kimi, code-reviewer-deepseek, and code-reviewer-minimax reviewers. Common constants gained deepseek, kimi, and legacy code-reviewer-lite model entries in FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS, while the waiting room now reports used (not remaining) premium sessions. BuffBench evaluations can target OpenCode via the new external:opencode agent ID and an OpenCodeRunner that spawns opencode run with JSON output (defaulting to opencode/kimi-k2.6 unless OPENCODE_MODEL overrides) and requires an OPENCODE_API_KEY.
ai.evidence: Commit 340fd17f bumps the version field from 1.0.671 to 1.0.672 in cli/release/package.json (the codebuff package), a single-line release-bump with the surrounding same-day commits shipping CLI login URL origin derivation, dynamic per-model agent selection, legacy code-reviewer-lite support, and the OpenCode BuffBench runner.

eli5.text: This release improves how you sign in, how your assistant picks the right AI model for a job, and how waiting rooms show your usage. You (or your team) now sign in through a more reliable login link that pulls the correct web address from your project settings instead of guessing the domain, so OAuth logins no longer bounce between the bare domain and the www version. The app is now smarter about matching your chosen model to the right built-in assistants: instead of one fixed setup, it dynamically selects the correct assistant for each model, adding dedicated review assistants tuned to Kimi, DeepSeek, and Minimax models, and it can automatically gate Gemini thinking steps when those models support it. Free-tier users gain additional model coverage, with DeepSeek and Kimi models now available alongside Minimax for free-mode tasks, while a legacy reviewer option is kept for older integrations. Finally, the waiting room now tells you how many of your daily premium sessions you have already used out of your total, and benchmark tooling gains an OpenCode runner so evaluations can include the OpenCode CLI with JSON output and model override support. Upgrading means more accurate logins, better model-specific behavior, clearer usage reporting, and broader model support in free mode, with no breaking changes to existing workflows.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.83 ships CLI login origin, dynamic model agents
ai.summary: Freebuff 0.0.83 is released, incrementing the version in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` from 0.0.82 to 0.0.83. This release bundles several user-visible improvements: the CLI login URL origin now derives from `NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL` (falling back to request origin or production domain) via a new `_origin.ts` helper, preventing apex/www host bouncing during OAuth; the CLI resolves freebuff agents dynamically based on the selected model through a new `freebuff-agent-selection.ts` utility, replacing the static `AGENT_MODE_TO_ID` lookup with model-specific root agents like `base2-free-deepseek` and `base2-free-kimi`; and OpenCode CLI was added as an external agent for BuffBench evaluations, spawning `opencode run` with JSON output defaulting to `opencode/kimi-k2.6`. Additional changes since 0.0.82 include adding `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL_ID` and `FREEBUFF_KIMI_MODEL_ID` to `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS`, allowing legacy `code-reviewer-lite` in free mode, switching the waiting room to display used premium sessions out of the total limit, and restoring subagent alias card matching by normalizing underscores to hyphens in `getAgentBaseName`.
ai.evidence: The diff hunk in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` changes the `version` field from `0.0.82` to `0.0.83`. The analysis notes confirm this is a `release-bump` commit bundling several prior user-visible changes dated 2026-05-07, including CLI login URL origin derivation from `NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL`, dynamic agent selection by model, free mode agent model additions, waiting room UI changes, and the OpenCode BuffBench runner.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.83 brings you better AI model selection, smarter CLI login behavior, and more accurate agent displays. The CLI now picks the right AI agent automatically based on which model you select, so DeepSeek users get DeepSeek-specific reviewers and Kimi users get Kimi-specific reviewers instead of one-size-fits-all agents. Login links now come from your configured app URL, preventing confusing redirects when you sign in from the terminal. The waiting room now shows how many premium sessions you have used out of your total, giving you a clearer picture of your daily limits. Subagent names now display correctly again after fixing underscore-to-hyphen normalization, and legacy code reviewer support ensures older clients still work. New OpenCode integration lets BuffBench evaluations run with OpenCode as an external agent option for broader testing coverage.

ai.title: CLI chat history deletion
ai.summary: Chat history screen adds delete action via `deleteChatSession` in `chat-history.ts`. `selectable-list.tsx` supports `actionLabel`/`onAction` props, replacing `Button` with `box` layout for row actions. Deletion validates `chatId` against path traversal, removes directory from `chats/`, and updates UI state immediately. Covers CLI only.

eli5.text: When you open your chat history in the command-line version of the assistant, each past conversation now has a delete option right next to it, so you can remove individual conversations without digging into folders. Pressing that delete button erases that conversation's saved files from your computer and immediately updates the list so the deleted entry disappears. The change only applies to the command-line tool, and the system checks the conversation name before deleting to prevent deleting files outside the conversations folder. This is available starting with version 1.0.670 of the command-line tool.
